item.title: Lotto win for lucky Athlone player
item.description: It's been a week to remember for one lucky lotto player in Athlone. A player scooped €250,000 in Wednesday's Lotto Plus 2 draw. The winner purchased their ticket on Tuesday 10th March at Circle K Athlone on the Dublin Road. Advertisement 06, 20, 22, 29, 30, 32 were the winning numbers. The bonus number was 15. The winner is advised to sign the back of their ticket and keep it safe and contact the Prize Claims team.

item.title: James Ryan missed Ireland clash with Scotland
item.description: James Ryan will miss Ireland’s showdown with Scotland on Saturday in the Aviva stadium. A calf issue, means Ryan was not considered as Joe McCarthy comes into the second row. Captain Caelan Doris leads Ireland into the Round 5 showdown. Jamie Osborne, Rob Baloucoune and Tommy O'Brien start in Ireland's back three, with Stuart McCloskey and Garry Ringrose once again named in the midfield, while Jamison Gibson-Park and Jack Crowley link up in the half-backs. item.title: Local MEP seeks meeting with Pieta CEO over Athlone centre closure
item.description: A local MEP has expressed his disappointment over the closure of Pieta House's centre in Athlone. News emerged this evening that the organisation's centre on Sean Costello Street in the Midlands town is set to close as its services move to an outreach model. The centre was established following extensive campaigning from local committees and over €120,000 raised for its development. item.title: Enoch Burke transfer from Castlerea Prison to be decided next week
item.description: The High Court has heard a decision to move Enoch Burke from Mountjoy to Castlerea Prison was lawful. The teacher will find out next week if his challenge against the transfer has been successful. On the 1st of March, Enoch Burke was moved from Mountjoy, where he had been detained since January, to Castlerea Prison. He has since argued this was in breach of a court order for his committal. item.description: Disgust has been expressed in Ballaghaderreen over the latest littering episode. Large quantities of litter and waste has been discovered at the rear of a house in the town. This follows another dumping incident in recent weeks at The Plots area. item.title: Roscommon driver with suspected false driving licence expected to face court
item.description: Two vehicles have been seized in Co Roscommon after separate traffic stops within the space of just over an hour on the same evening. The first driver was found to have no insurance and was also suspected to be a false driving licence. Gardaí have confirmed both the vehicle and the licence were seized at the scene. item.title: 'Justice at its best' - reaction to sentencing over Roscommon burglary spree
item.description: Yesterday's sentencing for a burglary spree in Roscommon is being described as 'an example of justice at its best'. Eugene Traynor, 48, with an address at Aderrig Square, Adamstown, Lucan, Co Dublin, was jailed for six and a half years. He was one of three people who burgled businesses in Frenchpark, Tulsk, Fourmilehouse and Knockcroghery in August 2024. item.title: 12 times as many holiday lets as long-term rental homes in Leitrim
item.description: There are over 12 times as many short-term lets in Co Leitrim than for long-term rental use. Threshold found 87 are available on Airbnb in the county - but just seven are available to rent on Daft.ie. The ratio isn't as bad in the other Shannonside counties - at 3 to 1 in Roscommon, and 1.2 to 1 in Longford. item.title: Man accused of New Year's Day assault in Ballagh due back in court today
item.description: A Ukrainian national accused of assault causing serious harm to an Englishman in Ballaghaderreen is due back in court today. Yevhen Shutko, 46, with an address in Loughglynn, west Roscommon, is charged with assault which led to the death of Jorden Newin on New Year's Day. Following the alleged incident, the 39-year-old was transferred to Sligo University Hospital and then to Beaumont Hospital, where he later died.
